claim.value: Complete histories do not prove the absence of unrecorded offline work.
claim.scope: An evidential limit concerning activity outside the record.

provenance.rationale: The cited span explicitly states this limit.

signal_basis.value: Linked account and schedule records, supplemented by customer follow-ups, yield an internally consistent history with reported offline activity distinguished from logged events and retrospective reports and unknowns explicitly labeled.
signal_basis.scope: A bounded cohort of new accounts; the proposed continuity signal is assumed observed for this judgment.

provenance.rationale: The bundle supplies the cohort boundary, linkage operation, treatment of offline reports, continuity signal and proposed status.
This supported evidential limit requires no unresolved empirical relation.

rationale: Internal continuity establishes consistency among recorded events, but cannot establish that every offline activity was recorded. Even successful linkage and follow-up therefore leave the possibility of unrecorded offline work open, licensing the stated limit.
uncertainty: Whether unrecorded offline work actually occurred remains unknown; the claim asserts only that complete histories cannot rule it out.
